questions.stem: A service streams a CSV report over a socket it keeps open for later messages. It builds `GZIPOutputStream gz = new GZIPOutputStream(socketOut)` and `BufferedWriter w = new BufferedWriter(new OutputStreamWriter(gz, UTF_8))`, writes 3,000 rows with `w.write(...)`, then calls `gz.finish()` and returns. What can the receiver do with the bytes it got?

options.text: Decompress them without an error and find the last rows missing, since rows still held by the writer never reached the compressor
options.says: finish() completes only what has reached the compressor; the writer above it still held the last rows, so the data is valid but short

options.text: Decompress them without an error and find every row, since finish() takes what the writer holds before it writes the trailer
options.says: finish() has no reference to the layers above it; it completes only what it has already received

options.text: Fail to decompress them, since finish() leaves the GZIP trailer in the writer's buffer until the writer is flushed
options.says: the trailer goes down into socketOut, the stream the compressor wraps; the writer sits above the compressor

options.text: Fail to decompress them, since GZIP data is only complete once the stream under the compressor has been closed
options.says: finish() writes the rest of the data and the trailer without closing the stream below

origin.section: finish() Completes the GZIP Data Without Closing, but Only What Has Reached the Compressor

questions.stem: A job writes 1,000,000 `long` values, one `writeLong` call each, into `new DataOutputStream(new GZIPOutputStream(new BufferedOutputStream(fileOut)))`. A profile shows most of the time in the `Deflater`. Which change makes the `Deflater` run fewer times?

options.text: Add a BufferedOutputStream between the GZIPOutputStream and the existing buffer, since the compressor then gets fewer writes
options.says: that buffer is below the compressor: it collects the compressor's output and changes nothing about the writes going into the Deflater

options.text: Add a BufferedOutputStream between the existing buffer and fileOut, since the compressor then gets fewer writes
options.says: a buffer under the compressor changes the writes into the file, not the writes the Deflater is given

options.text: Add a BufferedOutputStream between the DataOutputStream and the GZIPOutputStream, since the compressor then gets fewer writes
options.says: a buffer above the compressor turns many small writes into few large ones before they reach the Deflater

options.text: Enlarge the existing buffer between the GZIPOutputStream and fileOut, since the compressor then gets fewer writes
options.says: the existing buffer is below the compressor; a larger one cuts file writes, not the writes the Deflater is given

origin.section: Buffer Above the Compressor: the Order Decides How Many Calls Reach Each Layer

questions.stem: Per-client request counts live in a `ConcurrentHashMap<String, Long>`, wrapped in `AuditedMap extends AbstractMap`, which logs each write and forwards to the map the methods `AbstractMap` needs. Eight threads each call `counts.merge("client-7", 1L, Long::sum)` 10,000 times on the `AuditedMap`. What does `counts.get("client-7")` return afterwards?

options.text: Always 80,000, since merge goes to ConcurrentHashMap.merge, which locks the key for the whole get-and-put
options.says: AuditedMap doesn't override merge, so Map's default runs on the decorator and ConcurrentHashMap's merge is never called

options.text: Always 80,000, since the merge AbstractMap inherits locks the wrapper for the whole get-and-put
options.says: the default makes no guarantees about synchronization or atomicity; nothing holds a lock between its get and its put

options.text: Usually less than 80,000, since merge runs Map's get-and-put on the wrapper, with no lock between the two
options.says: the default merge runs on the decorator as separate get and put calls, so concurrent increments overwrite each other

options.text: Usually less than 80,000, since put on the wrapper runs outside ConcurrentHashMap's lock, so two puts can tear
options.says: each forwarded put is still one atomic put on the ConcurrentHashMap; the updates are lost between the get and the put

origin.section: A Decorator That Doesn't Override a Default Method Runs the Interface's Code, Not the Wrapped Object's

questions.stem: A registry keeps a `HashSet<Collection<String>>` of topic lists that are already subscribed. A client registers `Collections.synchronizedCollection(topics)` twice, with the same `topics` list object both times. How many entries does the set hold?

options.text: One, since both wrappers pass equals and hashCode on to the topics list
options.says: synchronizedCollection keeps Object's identity equals and hashCode; only the List, Set and Map wrappers forward them

options.text: One, since both calls return the same wrapper object for the same list
options.says: each call creates a new wrapper object around the list

options.text: Two, since both wrappers keep Object's equals and hashCode, and are two objects
options.says: a Collection wrapper can't tell whether its contents follow List or Set equality, so it keeps identity, and the two wrappers are two objects

options.text: Two, since both wrappers pass equals on to the list but keep Object's hashCode
options.says: synchronizedCollection forwards neither equals nor hashCode; both are Object's

origin.section: A Decorator Is Another Object: equals Is Forwarded Only Where the Interface Defines It
